claims.text: Small changes in the ratio of magnetic to non-magnetic elements can tune magnetic exchange interactions in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Small compositional changes can tune phase stability in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Composition-induced changes in exchange interactions and phase stability can modify the magnetic transition temperature.
Composition-induced changes in exchange interactions and phase stability can modify the magnetocaloric effect.
The proposed starting material is a single-phase, non-equiatomic HEA in a low-dimensional form.
Systematically varying the concentrations of magnetic 3d transition metals is a method for tuning the alloy's magnetic behavior.
Local atomic ordering and phase composition affect magnetic exchange pathways.
Phase structure is associated with longitudinal spin fluctuations and magnetic structure.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations affect phase stability.
Adjusting composition changes the balance between magnetic and non-magnetic interactions.
Adjusting composition changes the magnitude of longitudinal spin fluctuations.
Changes in exchange interactions and longitudinal spin fluctuations shift the Curie temperature.
Changes in exchange interactions and longitudinal spin fluctuations alter the magnetocaloric entropy change during a magnetic transition.
Varying magnetic-element concentration will produce a systematic shift in magnetic transition temperature.
Varying magnetic-element concentration will produce a measurable change in field-induced magnetocaloric entropy change.
Composition changes beyond the single-phase stability range may cause phase separation or secondary-phase formation.
Phase separation or secondary phases may degrade magnetocaloric performance.
The quantitative composition-property relationship remains insufficiently established and requires experimental validation.
